newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IRI says will clear debts by end 1997.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IRI says will clear debts by end 1997.

text.p: Italian state holding company IRI said it would clear its debts by the end of the year thanks to its ongoing privatisation programme.
"IRI's financial recovery will be complete within the year with debts reduced to zero as a result of disposals in progress," IRI director-general Pietro Ciucci told a conference.
He said the net value of the group would rise significantly due to expected increases in profits.
Ciucci confirmed that planned IRI sell-offs included that of motorway operator Autostrade, Aeroporti di Roma, Banca di Roma and ferry company Finmare.
He said the proposed disposal of troubled state airline Alitalia and engineering group Finmeccanica was more problematic.
"The real problem is not so much the sell-off itself, but to find an adequate value for (the companies) while simultaneously privatising them," he said.

IRI's debts stood at 3.6 trillion lire at the end of June. It made a profit of 184 million lire in 1996 after seven years of losses. Earlier this year it transferred telecom holding Stet to the Treasury.
